title: Mangrove change in northern Tarut Bay between Safwa and Ras Tanura: December 2017 to January 2026
data: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, 10 m, tile 39RUK: scene S2A_39RUK_20171219_0_L2A (19 December 2017, processing baseline 00.01, tile cloud 0.25%) and scene S2C_39RUK_20260106_0_L2A (6 January 2026, baseline 05.11, tile cloud 0.05%), read as windows of cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs through the Earth Search STAC API (Element 84, collection sentinel-2-l2a).
method: Picked two clear scenes in the same season (December and January) eight years apart and read an 11 × 14 km window (EPSG:32639) of the green, red, near-infrared and B11 bands.
An analysis zone drawn by the analyst around the lagoon and its shores (3,635 ha) leaves out the towns of Safwa and Ras Tanura and their gardens, so palms and gardens are not counted as mangrove.
Mangrove = NDVI ≥ 0.3 with MNDWI < 0 (vegetation standing above the water, not submerged seagrass or algae).
Gain = mangrove in 2026 only, loss = 2017 only.
limits: No field data exists, so no error matrix was computed, and the OpenStreetMap comparison is a proxy, not verification. The tide state is unknown on both dates, and the 2026 scene shows more submerged mudflat on the west of the lagoon, so low fringes may be counted or dropped with the tide. Most of the gain sits on stand edges one or two pixels wide, where co-registration between the scenes matters, so it may mean growth, denser canopy or misregistration.
